text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Financial services group Fortis pays ABN AMRO Dfl 2.5 billion for merchant bank MeesPierson. (p1)
- Group of prominent portfolio managers see Amsterdam's AEX index rising 10 percent to 680 points in 1997 after early year correction to around 555. (p1)
- Shareholders of transport group Nedlloyd and the European Commission give green light to merger of its container activities with those of P&O. (p1-3)
- ATA agricultural futures market to be sold to EOE Options Exchange which will merge with Amsterdam Stock Exchange into Amsterdam Exchanges from January 1. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm presents draft proposal to adapt budget to euro on January 1, 2002. (p1)
- Philips Electronics sells its 187 Videoland video rental shops to management. (p3)
- Technical wholesaler Eriks buys Gemanys's Heusinger & Salmon Gruppe. (p3)
- Chemicals firm DSM buys rival BASF's 50 pct stake in Chinese joint venture. (p4) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Talks continue on where to site second national airport. (p1)
- Loss-making airline Transavia, 80 pct owned by KLM, to restructure for first time in 30 years. (p2)
- Retailer V&D, a Vendex-unit, to open several new small department stores. (p2)
- Infrastructural investment will need Dfl 54 billion instead of the Dfl 27 billion budgeted, Transport Minister. (p3) TELEGRAAF
- PM Wim Kok sees scope for some tax cuts in 1998, the year of the next general election (p3)
- Business Travel International (BTI) to link up with U.S., British and Swiss travel firms to form Dfl 20 billion turnover group. (p13)
TROUW
- PM Wim Kok backs Social Affairs Minister Ad Melkert in coalition row over minimum wage. (p1)
- Senior coalition partner Labour's (PvdA) parliamentary group wants health minister to clarify role of Dutch firm in supplying toxic glycerine to Haiti causing death of 88 children. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch oil company NAM and construction firm Grootint to build North Sea production platform. (p11)
- Belgian PM Jean-Luc Dehaene calls for drugs "mini-summit" between France, Germany, Netherlands and Benelux partners. (p1)
- Weather agency says this Christmas could be the coldest this century. (p1)
- Ajax slump at home to PSV, go into winter-break in seventh place in Dutch first division. (p1)
